mainTopic: The payments and marriage rules of the אונס and the מפתה: צער, when the fine is paid, refusing the marriage, and the כתובה
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא. In it, רבי שמעון says a rapist owes nothing for צער, since every wife feels that pain anyway, and the sages answer that forced relations are not like willing ones. רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה then defines the צער as the pain of having her legs spread by force. The גמרא asks why a מפתה does not pay this too. A parable about tearing someone's silk is rejected because the money belongs to her father. The final answer is that a willing girl feels hardly any pain, and three אמוראים quote women describing how mild it is. Next the גמרא rereads the משנה's rule on when the מפתה pays. It also discusses how both the girl and her father can refuse marriage to an אונס or a מפתה, with אביי and רבא giving different sources for the father's right. A second ברייתא explains that the wife of an אונס gets no more money if she leaves, and the רבנן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue over whether she gets a כתובה, depending on why a כתובה exists. The amud ends as רבא מפרזקיא begins a question to רב אשי about the rule that an אונס must keep her, and the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Ending of the view that the rapist owes nothing for pain
steps.stepSummary: The text opens at the end of a cited opinion: the אונס does not pay for צער, because she would feel that pain with her husband anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...since in the end she will suffer this pain anyway with her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא that began on the previous amud. In it, רבי שמעון says the rapist does not pay for צער, because every married woman goes through this pain anyway. The ברייתא was brought to challenge the earlier definition of צער as the pain of being thrown on the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is that the pain of first relations is not a real loss caused by the אונס. She would have gone through it with her husband in any case. The next step will push back on this.

keyTerms.meaning: Pain; one of the payments a rapist owes
Literally 'under her husband'; when she is married

phrases.english: since in the end she will suffer [this pain] under her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא (רבי שמעון's view) cited on the previous amud to challenge אבוה דשמואל's definition of צער
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אונס does not pay צער, because a woman feels this pain with her husband anyway

steps.title: Forced relations are not like willing relations
steps.stepSummary: The other sages answer that the pain of forced relations cannot be compared to willing relations with a husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: A woman who has relations by force is not comparable to one who has relations willingly.
steps.whatsHappening: The sages reject the argument from step 1. Forced relations hurt in a different way than willing relations with a husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument in step 1 assumed that the pain is the same in both cases. The sages say it is not: force adds real pain of its own. So the אונס does owe for צער.

phrases.english: They said to him:
A woman who has relations by force is not comparable
to one who has relations willingly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה נִבְעֶלֶת בְּאוֹנֶס לְנִבְעֶלֶת בְּרָצוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning of step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that a rapist owes no צער
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly treats forced relations and willing relations as causing the same pain

steps.title: The pain is the pain of being forced to spread her legs
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה defines the צער: it is the pain of having her legs forced apart, and he brings a פסוק that uses this wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: it is the pain of spreading her legs. And the פסוק also says, 'And you spread your legs to every passerby.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final definition of the צער that the אונס pays for. It is the pain of being forced into position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that both sides are talking about a pain that comes from the relations themselves, not from being thrown on the ground. So the earlier definition from the previous amud is dropped (אלא). The צער is the spreading of her legs, which a wife also goes through, but step 2 explained that force makes it a different pain. The פסוק shows this is a known way to describe the act.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Naḥman said
that Rabba bar Avuh said:
It is the pain of spreading the legs.
And so the verse says:
"And you spread your legs
to every passerby."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected definition from the previous amud with a new one that fits the ברייתא in steps 1-2
steps.terutzMaskana: The צער is the pain of spreading her legs during the forced act
steps.whatToRemember: The אונס pays for צער because the pain comes from the force itself, not from first relations in general.

steps.title: Then a seducer should pay for pain too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if this is the pain, a מפותה (seduced girl) should also get paid for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a seduced girl too [should be paid for pain]!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a מפתה does not pay for צער too. His victim also has her legs spread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the pain is simply the spreading of the legs, it happens in seduction too. But the halacha is that a מפתה does not pay צער. So the גמרא needs to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: A seduced girl, who took part willingly

phrases.english: If so, a seduced girl too!
phrases.notes: He means she should also be paid for this pain, but the halacha is that she is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition given in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר אבוה's definition of צער
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same leg-spreading happens in seduction, yet a מפתה does not pay צער

steps.title: A parable: tear my silk and you are free
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה compares the seduced girl to someone who tells another person to tear his silk with no payment owed. Since she agreed, she gave up the claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: What is the case of a seduced girl like? Like a person who said to his friend, 'Tear my silk, and you are free from paying.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer is a parable. A seduced girl agreed to the act, so she gave up any claim for the pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an owner allows damage to his own property, the one who does the damage owes nothing. The idea is that her agreement cancels the payment for צער.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
A parable for the seduced girl: what is the matter like?
To a person who said to his friend:
Tear my silk and be free from paying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Waiver: she gave up her own claim
steps.terutzMaskana: The seduced girl agreed, so she gave up the payment

steps.title: It is not her silk; it belongs to her father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the parable. The payments of a young girl belong to her father, so she cannot give them up.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'My' silk? It belongs to her father!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the parable. The girl is not the owner of this payment; her father is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving up a claim only works when you own it. Since these payments go to the father, her agreement cannot cancel them. So the waiver idea does not explain why the מפתה owes nothing.

phrases.english: "My" silk?! They are her father's!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the parable from step 5
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: She cannot give up money that belongs to her father

steps.title: A seduced girl feels no real pain
steps.stepSummary: A new answer from רבה בר אבוה: the wise women say a girl who takes part willingly has no pain, so there is nothing to pay for.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the wise women among them say that a seduced girl has no pain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a better answer. There is no צער payment for a מפותה because she does not really feel pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not rely on her giving up a claim. It says the loss itself is missing, so the father has nothing to collect either.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
The clever women among them say:
A seduced girl has no pain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: פִּקְּחוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶן אוֹמְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 5
steps.terutzMaskana: A willing girl does not feel pain, so there is no צער to pay

steps.title: But we see that there is pain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: experience shows that a woman does feel pain the first time, even willingly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't we see that she does have pain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 7 from real life. Willing first relations also seem to cause pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it is well known that first relations hurt even with consent, the claim that a seduced girl feels nothing seems wrong.

phrases.english: But don't we see that she has [pain]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a seduced girl has no pain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Experience shows pain exists even in willing first relations

steps.title: Three women describe the pain as mild
steps.stepSummary: אביי, רבא, and רב פפא each report what a woman told them: willing first relations bring only a small, passing discomfort.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My mother told me it is like hot water on a bald man's head. רבא said: The daughter of רב חסדא told me it is like the prick of a bloodletting lancet. רב פפא said: The daughter of אבא סוראה told me it is like hard bread on the gums.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים answer the challenge. Each quotes a woman who says the pain of willing relations is tiny and quick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each image describes a quick sting that passes, not real suffering. So when the wise women said 'no pain' in step 7, they meant no pain worth paying for. That explains why a מפתה owes no צער.

keyTerms.meaning: The prick of a bloodletting lancet

phrases.english: Abaye said: My mother told me:
phrases.notes: This is the woman who raised אביי; he often quotes her this way.

phrases.english: Like hot water on the head of a bald man.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲמַרָה לִי בַּת רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rava said: The daughter of Rav Ḥisda told me:
Like the prick of a bloodletting lancet.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֲמַרָה לִי בַּת אַבָּא סוּרָאָה:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The daughter of Abba of Sura told me:
Like hard bread on the gums.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying that the pain is too small to count
steps.terutzMaskana: Willing relations cause only a slight, passing discomfort, so the מפתה pays no צער
steps.whatToRemember: The אונס pays צער because force causes real pain. The מפתה does not, because willing relations cause only a tiny, passing discomfort.

steps.title: How can the seducer 'send her away' if she is not his wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the rapist pays right away, and the seducer pays when he sends her away. It asks how that can be, since she is not his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] The rapist pays immediately; the seducer pays when he sends her away, etc. 'When he sends her away'? Is she his wife?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and questions its wording. 'Sending away' sounds like divorce, but the seducer never married her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word used for sending away normally means divorcing a wife. A seducer has no marriage to end, so the wording looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: When he sends her away (language used for divorce)

phrases.english: The rapist gives immediately,
the seducer when he sends her away, etc.
"When he sends her away"?! Is she his wife?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Divorce language does not fit a man who never married her

steps.title: Read it as 'when he does not marry her'
steps.stepSummary: אביי says to read the משנה as 'when he does not marry her.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Say instead, 'when he does not marry her.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי fixes the wording of the משנה. The seducer pays only if he ends up not marrying her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gives the seducer a chance to marry the girl. If he marries her, he pays no קנס. If he does not marry her, he must pay it.

keyTerms.meaning: When he does not marry her

phrases.english: Abaye said: Say "when he does not marry her."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 10
steps.terutzMaskana: The seducer pays the קנס only if he does not marry her

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי and adds that בושת and פגם are paid right away
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא uses אביי's exact wording and adds that the payments for shame and loss of value are paid right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא too: Even though they said the seducer pays when he does not marry her, the payments for shame and loss of value he pays immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says 'when he does not marry her,' just like אביי. The ברייתא also limits which payments wait.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the קנס waits to see if he marries her. בושת (shame) and פגם (loss of value) are paid right away no matter what.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Even though they said
the seducer gives when he does not marry her,
shame and loss of value he gives immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's reading from step 11
steps.raayaObject: אביי's reading 'when he does not marry her'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses the same wording
steps.whatToRemember: Only the seducer's קנס depends on whether he marries her. בושת and פגם are always paid right away.

steps.title: Both the girl and her father can refuse the marriage
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: with both the rapist and the seducer, the girl or her father can block the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whether it is the rapist or the seducer, both she and her father can prevent the marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more rule. The man cannot force the marriage; the girl or her father may refuse it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's command to marry her binds the man, not the girl. Either she or her father can say no.

keyTerms.meaning: Both the rapist and the seducer

phrases.english: And whether the rapist or the seducer,
both she and her father
are able to prevent [the marriage].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶחָד הָאוֹנֵס וְאֶחָד הַמְפַתֶּה, בֵּין הִיא וּבֵין אָבִיהָ יְכוֹלִין לְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With both the אונס and the מפתה, the girl or her father may refuse the marriage

steps.title: Granted: the seducer case has a verse for both father and girl
steps.stepSummary: For the מפתה, the פסוק 'אם מאן ימאן' teaches that the father can refuse, and the doubled word teaches that the girl can refuse too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, with a seduced girl it is written: 'If her father utterly refuses.' That only tells me about her father. From where do I know about the girl herself? The verse says 'refuses' in a doubled way, meaning in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its question by first showing the easy case: the מפתה, where a פסוק covers both people. This 'granted' line prepares the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said both the girl and her father can block the marriage. For the מפתה, the פסוק names the father outright. The doubled verb מאן ימאן adds the girl as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this part is fine (sets up a question about the next part)
A girl who was seduced (she agreed)

phrases.english: Granted, with a seduced girl, it is written:
"If her father utterly refuses."
I only know this about her father;
from where do we know it about the girl herself?
The verse says "refuses," meaning in any case.
phrases.notes: The verb is doubled (מָאֵן יְמָאֵן), so the extra word adds that she can refuse too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts looking for the sources behind the ברייתא's rule in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the מפתה, both the father and the girl can block the marriage, based on 'אם מאן ימאן'.

steps.title: For the rapist, where does the father's right come from?
steps.stepSummary: For the אונס, the girl's right comes from 'ולו תהיה'. But no פסוק has been given for the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a rapist? Granted, she herself can refuse, as it is written 'And to him she shall be,' meaning with her consent. But from where do we know that her father can refuse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source that lets the father block marriage to an אונס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ולו תהיה' ('she shall be his') are read as 'only if she agrees,' so the girl's right is covered. The פסוק says nothing about the father, so his right still needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who forced himself on a girl
And to him she shall be (as a wife)

phrases.english: But a rapist, from where?
Granted for her, it is written:
"And to him she shall be," meaning with her consent.
But her father, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the easy case (מפתה) to the hard case (אונס).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for the father's right to block marriage to the אונס.

steps.title: אביי: a sinner should not profit
steps.stepSummary: אביי says no פסוק is needed. If the father could not refuse, the אונס would gain something by sinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: so that a sinner should not profit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers with logic instead of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal man cannot marry a girl if her father refuses. If the אונס could marry her against her father's will, his sin would give him a right that others do not have. So the father must be able to refuse.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner who profits from his sin

phrases.english: Abaye said:
So that a sinner should not profit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father's right comes from the principle that a sinner must not profit.

steps.title: רבא: a קל וחומר from the seducer
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns it from a קל וחומר. The מפתה only went against the father, and still both can refuse. The אונס went against both of them, so surely both can refuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is a קל וחומר. A seducer went against only her father's will, and still both she and her father can block the marriage. A rapist went against both her father's will and her own will. All the more so they can both block it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer, using a קל וחומר (an 'all the more so' argument).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מפתה is the 'lighter' case, since the girl agreed. The אונס is the 'heavier' case, since he went against everyone. If the father can refuse in the lighter case, he can surely refuse in the heavier one.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'all the more so' argument from a lighter case to a heavier one
Is it not all the more so?

phrases.english: Rava said: it is a kal vachomer:
If a seducer, who did not go against
anyone's will except her father's,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הִיא וּבֵין אָבִיהָ יְכוֹלִין לְעַכֵּב —
phrases.english: can be blocked by both her and her father,
then a rapist, who went against her father's will

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דַּעַת עַצְמָהּ, לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?!
phrases.english: and against her own will, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 15, different from אביי's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father's right comes from a קל וחומר from the מפתה.

steps.title: Why רבא rejects אביי: the rapist pays a fine
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that the אונס does not profit, because he pays the קנס anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא did not say like אביי, because since the rapist pays the fine, he is not a sinner who profits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא did not accept אביי's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אונס must pay the קנס of fifty silver pieces even when he marries her. So he gains nothing from his sin, and אביי's principle does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed fine set by the Torah

phrases.english: Rava did not say like Abaye.
Since he pays the fine,
he is not a sinner who profits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבא needed his own answer instead of אביי's.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The אונס pays the קנס, so he does not actually profit.

steps.title: Why אביי rejects רבא: the rapist cannot back out
steps.stepSummary: אביי breaks the קל וחומר. With the מפתה, everyone, including the man himself, can block the marriage. With the אונס, the man cannot block it, so maybe the father cannot either.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי did not say like רבא. A seducer can himself block the marriage, so her father can also block it. A rapist cannot himself block the marriage, so maybe her father also cannot block it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי did not accept רבא's קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אונס is in one way stricter: the Torah forces him to marry her if she wants. That points to a rule that the marriage cannot be blocked at all, which could include the father. So the אונס is not simply a 'heavier' version of the מפתה, and the קל וחומר does not work.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that the father can block marriage to the אונס. אביי learns it from 'a sinner should not profit.' רבא learns it from a קל וחומר from the מפתה. Each rejects the other's reasoning: the אונס pays the קנס anyway, and the אונס himself cannot back out.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the father really cannot block the marriage. He is only showing why the קל וחומר fails; his own reason, 'a sinner should not profit,' still gives the father that right.

phrases.english: Abaye did not say like Rava:
a seducer, who himself can block the marriage,
her father can also block it;
a rapist, who himself cannot block the marriage,
her father also cannot block it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 18 and explains why אביי needed his own answer instead of רבא's.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's קל וחומר from the מפתה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The אונס is stricter in a way that cuts against the father: the man himself cannot block the marriage, so it may be that no one can.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: the אונס pays right away and owes nothing more
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the אונס pays the קנס immediately, and when 'he' sends her out she has no further claim on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: Even though they said that an אונס pays right away, when he sends her out, she has no claim on him at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the money an אונס owes. It says he pays the fine at once, and later, when the marriage ends, she gets nothing more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the אונס pays the fine right away, unlike the מפתה, who pays only if he does not marry her. The ברייתא adds that because she was already paid, she has no extra money coming when the marriage ends. But the words 'when HE sends her out' will cause a problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: She has no claim on him at all

phrases.english: Another ברייתא taught:
Even though they said
that a rapist pays right away,
when he sends her out,
she has no claim on him at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about the money side of the אונס's marriage, after the earlier discussion about who can refuse it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אונס pays the קנס immediately, and when the marriage ends she has no further monetary claim.

steps.title: How can the אונס send her out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording 'when he sends her out': an אונס is never allowed to divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'When he sends her out'?! Can he send her out?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of the ברייתא. The Torah forbids the אונס to ever divorce her, so how can the ברייתא talk about him sending her out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says about the אונס that he may not send her away all his days. So a case where he divorces her should be impossible. The problem is only with the wording, not with the money rule itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Is he able? (a challenge: surely he can't)

phrases.english: When he sends her out?!
Can he send her out?!
phrases.notes: The Torah says the אונס may never divorce her (דברים 22:29).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'כשיוציא הוא' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אונס is forbidden by the Torah to divorce her, so a case of him sending her out cannot happen.

steps.title: Fix the wording: when SHE leaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading to 'when she leaves': if she asks to end the marriage, she has no claim on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: when she leaves, she has no claim on him at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the wording. The ברייתא means that if she is the one who wants to leave, she gets nothing more from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He cannot divorce her on his own, but if she wants out, he can give her a גט. In that case she gets no more money, because she already got the fine at the start. The rule stays, and only the case becomes one where she starts the divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (the גמרא fixes the wording)

phrases.english: Say instead:
when she leaves,
she has no claim on him at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by changing 'he sends her out' to 'she leaves.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to describe the אונס divorcing her, which is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about her choosing to leave, and then she has no further claim.

steps.title: If he dies: the fine counts as her כתובה, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagrees
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if the אונס dies, the fine she got takes the place of her כתובה. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says she also gets a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he died, the money of her fine stands in place of her כתובה. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: she has a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on to the case where the אונס dies. The first opinion says she gets nothing more, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says she gets a כתובה of one hundred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion holds that the fine she already got counts as her כתובה, so no extra payment is due. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says that on top of the fine she gets a regular כתובה of a מנה, like any woman who was not a בתולה at marriage. This sets up the question of what they really argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: Her fine money stands in place of her כתובה
One hundred זוז, the כתובה of a woman who was not a בתולה

phrases.english: If he died,
the money of her fine goes in place of her ketubah.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
She has a ketubah of a maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the case of death and brings a disagreeing opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: the fine counts as her כתובה. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: she also gets a כתובה of a מנה.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle the two opinions in the ברייתא are arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the two opinions disagree. This short question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants the reasoning behind each side, not just the rulings. It is looking for the basic idea each side holds.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the מחלוקת just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that splits the רבנן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why a כתובה exists, and whether it applies here
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say a כתובה only exists to stop a quick divorce, and the אונס cannot divorce her. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he can still torment her until she asks to leave, so she needs a כתובה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: Why did the Sages set up the כתובה? So that it should not be easy in his eyes to divorce her. And this man cannot divorce her anyway. And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds: this man too can make her miserable until she says 'I don't want you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both sides. They agree on why a כתובה exists, but they disagree on whether that reason fits the wife of an אונס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say a כתובה is a 'price tag' on divorce, and the אונס is forbidden to divorce her, so she needs no כתובה. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the danger is still there, because he can make her life so hard that she asks for a גט. The כתובה protects her from that.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages set up (a rabbinic rule)
Easy in his eyes to divorce her
He torments her, makes her miserable

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a כתובה is there so divorce will not be easy. The רבנן say the אונס can't divorce anyway, so no כתובה. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he can push her to ask for a divorce, so she still needs one.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
What is the reason the Sages set up the ketubah?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא קַלָּה בְּעֵינָיו לְהוֹצִיאָהּ,
phrases.english: So that it should not be easy in his eyes to divorce her,
and this man cannot divorce her anyway.
And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda holds:
this one too can make her miserable
until she says, "I don't want you."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: טַעְמָא מַאי תַּקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by giving each side's reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They agree a כתובה exists to make divorce costly. The רבנן say the אונס can't divorce her, so it isn't needed. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he can torment her into asking for a divorce, so it is needed.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבא מפרזקיא begins a question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'אונס שותה בעציצו', and רבא מפרזקיא starts a question to רב אשי, based on the fact that the laws of אונס and מפתה are learned from each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'An אונס drinks from his pot.' רבא מפרזקיא said to רב אשי: Since they learn from each other,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line in the משנה. רבא מפרזקיא begins a question, and this step only lays down his starting point; the question itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the אונס must marry her and keep her, but the מפתה does not have to. רבא מפרזקיא starts from the idea that the laws of אונס and מפתה are learned from one another. He is getting ready to ask why this rule is not shared too.

keyTerms.meaning: Drinks from his pot (must keep the wife he got this way)
Since, after all (opens a line of reasoning)
They are learned from each other
רבא from the town of Parzakya

phrases.english: "A rapist drinks from his pot."
phrases.notes: These are words from our משנה: the אונס must marry her and keep her, like drinking from the pot he chose.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזִקְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava from Parzakya said to Rav Ashi:
Since they are learned from each other,
phrases.notes: He means the laws of אונס and מפתה, like the amount of the fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כתובה discussion and turns to a new phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The question is not finished here. It is built on the idea that אונס and מפתה share laws, so the next lines will ask why this rule is different.
